scope: Only precomputing a Set of design module IDs and replacing repeated Array.some membership checks in causal log affectedIds validation.
reasoning: For string module identifiers the Set.has membership predicate has the same equality result as the former strict-equality Array.some predicate. The preceding typeof id === string requirement is retained, as are the error kind, code and message.

The Set is created once per synchronous validation call from the same design.modules inventory. It does not persist across calls, change module order, modify the caller, or alter authoritative state. It replaces repeated linear membership scans with a per-call inventory construction and lookups. No measured speedup is claimed.
Existing affectedIds array/size and structural checks are unchanged. Empty and duplicate valid scopes retain prior admission; this optimization does not silently impose a new log contract.

commands.result: Review harness virtual TypeScript module was not transpiled by Vite; parse stopped before semantic probes ran. No product source or expectation changed.
12 of 12 comparative probes passed after explicitly transpiling the prior TypeScript validator in the review harness.

limitations: Review covers this exact two-line optimization only. The lead owns lint, product test suites and the complete clean committed gate.

Comparative probes use an engine-generated two-module state. The original validator is read from the baseline Git blob, its relative module paths are adapted to the current unchanged dependencies, and TypeScript types are erased for an isolated module loader. There are no numerical mocks.
No browser/server port, remote operation, commit, production source edit or historical file edit was performed. No performance benchmark was run.
outcome: PASS: the reviewed optimization preserves causal-scope admission and rejection semantics in source and all 12 executed comparative cases.
